contract.interface:
For a strongly connected loopless digraph G with adjacency B, N>=2 and spectral radius r>0, replace each vertex by the transitive tournament T_m and each original arc by all cross-block arcs. The source derives rho(B tensor J_m + I_N tensor T_m)=1/((1+1/r)^(1/m)-1), preservation of directed girth and delta-plus(G[T_m])=m delta-plus(G). For D_m=C4[T_m], rho(D_5)>20/3 although girth=4, and rho(D_m)/(4m)->1/(4 log 2)>1/3. These graphs have minimum outdegree density 1/4: they refute the proposed spectral implication, not Caccetta–Häggkvist. The substitution construction is acknowledged prior mathematics; originality of the calculation is unestablished.

Define beta(M)=max_{w>=0,1^T w=1} min_i (Mw)_i=min_{p in Delta} max_j (M^T p)_j. For nonempty finite blocks H_i, the source proves beta(G[H_1,...,H_n])=beta(A_G+diag(beta(A_Hi))). Acyclic blocks have beta=0, so acyclic substitution preserves beta even for unequal block sizes; beta(D_m)=1/4. This distinguishes distinct-neighbour mass from walk growth and supplies no universal one-third bound.

On Z/10, include increments +1,+3 everywhere and +2 where i mod 5 is in {0,1,3}. The source gives girth four, det A=5, w=(3,1,2,2,1,3,1,2,2,1)/18 and p=(2,2,1,3,1,2,2,1,3,1)/18, with Aw=A^T p=(5/18)1. Positivity plus invertibility gives unique optimizers p!=w. This excludes identifying the two optimal measures; it does not exclude every weighted or stationary method.

The remaining assertion is beta(A+I/3)<=1/3 for every finite triangle-free oriented adjacency A, equivalently for every w in Delta some i obeys (Aw)_i<=(1-w_i)/3. The response derives equivalence to the directed-triangle Caccetta–Häggkvist target, using lexicographic powers of C4, continuity and rational independent-clone blowups. The assertion itself is unproved. Computing or naming beta has not removed the original obstruction.

Inputs/costs: explicit finite adjacency matrices, graph substitutions and simplex optimization; no efficient universal triangle certificate or new complexity bound is established. N618 is a separately sourced earlier failure of a stationary-neighbourhood inequality, mentioned only as background; neither its script nor OpenAI/math formalizations were replayed here. The intermediate progress line about cubic Gibbs observables is retained as transcript data and is not promoted to a separate result. The source explicitly reports that its major foundational completion standard was not met.
